collections.title: Seven days with death
collections.intro: One short talk and one practice a day for a week. The traditions agree on little, but they agree that remembering death changes how we live. Go gently; skip a day whenever you need to.
collections.author: Satsang

units.title: The one certainty
units.intro: Start with the plain fact: everyone who is born dies.

items.note: What would I stop putting off if I took this seriously?

units.title: Who dies?
units.intro: Advaita turns the question around: find who it is that is afraid.

units.title: Grief and loss

units.title: Practising dying

units.title: What remains
units.intro: End where the traditions point: the deathless, the Self, the open sky of mind.

collections.intro: Does anything carry on after death? One talk from each tradition that answers, then the classic texts to read for free.

collections.title: Kashmir Shaivism: a first syllabus
collections.intro: The nondual Śaiva tradition of Kashmir, in six steps: a theory track of short talks from scholars and teachers, and a practice track of simple contemplations from the Vijñāna Bhairava and the Pratyabhijñā.

collections.title: Thai Forest: the basics
collections.intro: The forest tradition of Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah, as its Western monks teach it today: virtue, the breath, Buddho, walking, and how to bring it into a life.

collections.title: Visualisations: the Tibetan deity practice primer
collections.intro: Orientation only. Deity yoga is taught in Tibetan Buddhism after an empowerment and with a teacher; this primer explains what it is and why it is practised, through talks by teachers of the tradition. It does not teach the visualisations themselves.

collections.title: Metta in four traditions
collections.intro: Goodwill, loving-kindness, compassion: four ways of growing a kind heart, one sit at a time.

collections.title: How to discern past lives
collections.caution: Orientation only, not instruction. In the Pa-Auk method, discerning past lives requires deep jhāna and a qualified teacher, typically on a long retreat. The foundation offered here, mindfulness of breathing, is real and safe for anyone. Stop if anything in this course becomes distressing.
collections.stepCaution: A reminder at every step: rebirth and the recollection of past lives are central to these traditions, but they are not independently verified. No results are promised. Stop if any of this becomes distressing.
collections.intro: What the Pa-Auk tradition claims about seeing past lives, how rebirth-linking works in its Abhidhamma, which kamma and craving shape a next life, and why futures seen in meditation are possibilities, not destinies. Then a comparative arm from Kashmir Shaivism, the evidence question, and where both traditions end: liberation now. Six sessions, fifteen talks, a breath practice that is safe for anyone, and honest orientation on the rest.

units.title: The Pa-Auk claims
units.listenFor: Listen for exactly what is claimed: that after deep concentration a meditator can discern mind and matter in earlier lives, and that the method treats this as part of understanding dependent origination, never as a goal. Notice how the second talk handles belief.

items.note: The fullest statement of what the method claims, from a nun trained at Pa-Auk (68 min).

units.title: Kashmir Shaivism on karma and rebirth
units.listenFor: A comparative arm. Listen for how Kashmir Shaivism tells the story differently: one consciousness contracting itself into a limited being by its own power, with karma among the impurities that keep the contraction going, and rebirth as that contraction continuing.

units.title: The evidence question
units.listenFor: Listen for how a careful scholar treats evidence: what the early texts actually say, what research on rebirth claims can and cannot show. Then hear the method's founder as a primary source. Hold both without forcing a verdict.

items.note: A scholar-monk on the early texts and current research, with two Harvard respondents (2 h 15).

units.title: Liberation now
units.listenFor: Both traditions end in the same place: the point is not to collect past lives but to be free now. Listen for "liberation is not somewhere else" and for what sudden awakening means.
